source.notes: ICSE Class 7 school first-semester examination paper, English Paper 1 (school not named). Header prints '1st SEMESTER EXAMINATION, 2022 -2023', 'CLASS 7', 'ENGLISH PAPER - 1', 'MARKS 25', 'TIME : 1½ HRS.'; examYear 2023 is the later year of the printed session (the file name also carries 080823 and 2023); durationMinutes 90 = 1½ hours as printed. The PDF is a skewed photocopy scan with no text layer (watermark only); text was OCRed with RapidOCR and corrected against the page images. Section A: I composition [3] (two options, OR), II letter/application [3] (OR; alternatives labelled (a)/(b) by the editor), III comprehension [4] (marks printed for the whole group, kept as one entry with the passage, which is under 250 words). Section B grammar groups print marks only per group. On page 2 the mark brackets ([3], [3], [2], [2]) are printed in the gaps between groups; each is assigned to the group heading just below it (II, III, IV, V), which leaves Section B I with no printed mark (flagged, confidence LOW). With that reading the printed marks add up to 20, not the printed 25; the bracket positions are ambiguous and should be checked against the scan. A pen mark overwrites '2)' in Section B II; the word 'Play' before item II 1) is struck through on the scan. The paper's own spellings ('given-below', 'top many', 'contious', 'reach station') are kept. Section B groups are numbered I-V on the paper, the same numerals as Section A; they are stored as B-I … B-V to keep numbers unique. Section B I carries marks 0 as a placeholder. No answer key is printed; no official answers exist.

questions.text:
Read the passage given-below and answer the questions that follow:
The culture of nuclear families is in fashion. Parents are often heard complaining about the difficulties in bringing up children these days. Too much of freedom in demand, too much independence; over night parties: excessive extravagance, splurging pocket money; no time for studies and family all this is a common cry of such families. Aren't parents, themselves, responsible for this pitiful state ? The basic need of a growing youth is the family, love, attention and bonding along with moral values. One should not forget that 'charity begins at home'. Independence and individuality both need to be respected, in order to maintain the sanctity of family. Children, today are to be handled with tact in order to bridge the ever widening generation gap. Only the reasonable demands need to be fulfilled, as there are too many expenses to be met and top many social obligations to be taken care of by the parents. Our forefathers lived happily in joint families. Children loved to live with their cousins, learnt to adjust within means. There was perfect harmony between the generations. There never existed the concept of old-age homes. There was deep respect for the family elders and love, care and concern for the youngsters. Even the minor family differences were solved amicably.
1) Mention Any 2 major concerns of a nuclear family.
2) Who according to the passage, are responsible for them?
3) Describe the atmosphere in joint families.
4) Which word in the passage means 'Holiness of life'?
extractionIssues: Marks printed only for the whole group ([4] for four questions)
Question labels 3) and 4) are partly cut off at the page edge on the scan
